summary:
Space Tiger Health Assistant is a local-first prototype that brings astronaut health information into one understandable view. It combines daily check-ins and fictional health readings with NASA-informed resources to make health context easier to explore.

The dashboard connects trends, body context, and explainable findings. Clinical Quality Language rules show why supported findings appear, while an evidence library provides background sources. Daily routines and reminders support follow-through, and Scenario Lab lets users preview changes without altering saved observations. Mobile views and a wearable reminder demonstration extend the experience across devices.

By bringing observations, explanations, and daily support together, the project explores how crews could maintain a clearer picture of health during missions.

All profiles and readings are fictional. The prototype is not a medical device or medical advice, has no connected sensors or backend, and has not been validated or endorsed by NASA. The watch notification is shown in an emulator.
details:
Space Tiger Health Assistant brings health observations, daily wellbeing, and mission context together in a single view. It is designed to help crews explore information, understand findings, and keep daily routines in sight.

The dashboard presents trends and a body navigator alongside explainable findings. Rules written in Clinical Quality Language connect supported readings to explanations and evidence. The Scenario Lab lets users explore how changes affect the preview without modifying saved observations. Mobile views and reminders extend the experience beyond the dashboard.

Our creative approach combines a whole-person view with transparent reasoning: users can explore not only what appears, but why. We considered clarity, local-first operation, accessibility across devices, and the need to distinguish illustrative findings from medical decisions.

NASA’s human-performance, medical-operations, and Human Research Program resources informed the evidence and context. We developed the project with React, TypeScript, Vite, Clinical Quality Language, and Capacitor, using Android emulation and GitHub Pages. AI assistance supported development and video narration.

Limitations: Profiles, readings, and plans are fictional. There are no connected sensors or backend, and local sign-in is not authentication. Example ranges are not clinical or safety limits. The watch notification is shown in an emulator; physical delivery is unverified. The prototype is not a medical device or medical advice and has not been validated or endorsed by NASA.
